records.source_observation: The publisher's first 2024-labelled English item asks who passed Salma the notes she called the Note of Salvation.
records.independent_reasoning: Kolawole was the student beside Salma who passed her the notes during the examination. 'Notes of Salvation' was Salma's name for those notes.

records.source_observation: The publisher compares the rhyme of boys against moist, elbows, noise and stays; its selected option is noise.
records.independent_reasoning: Boys and noise both end in /ɔɪz/. Moist ends in /ɔɪst/, while elbows and stays have different vowel sounds.

records.source_observation: The publisher tests the main stress of productivity with four visibly marked syllable patterns.
records.independent_reasoning: The main stress falls on the syllable 'tiv': produc-TIV-i-ty. The earlier 'prod' has only secondary stress.

records.source_observation: The publisher marks the u in busy and offers vineyard, automobile, twilight and island as comparisons.
records.independent_reasoning: The first vowel in busy is /ɪ/, as in the first syllable of vineyard. Twilight and island begin with /aɪ/ instead.

records.source_observation: The publisher's novel item asks where the narrator and her children sat because the room was stuffy.
records.independent_reasoning: Jamila suggested moving outside to the mango tree in the courtyard, and the family went there.

records.source_observation: The publisher marks the th in clothe and contrasts it with cloth, smooth, good and thesis.
records.independent_reasoning: Clothe and smooth end in /ð/. Cloth and thesis use /θ/, while good ends in /d/.

records.source_observation: The publisher asks why the quiet character received the name Talle, distinct from why villagers called him quiet.
records.independent_reasoning: The novel links Talle's name to his mother's death soon after he was born. His reticent behaviour explains his later nickname, 'the quiet one'.
records.independently_selected_answer: His mother died shortly after his birth

records.source_observation: The publisher's completion item includes the word of after the blank and contrasts Despite with In spite.
records.independent_reasoning: 'In spite of' expresses the intended contrast. The word 'of' is already in the sentence, so 'despite of' would be ungrammatical.
